SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 gives deg W_{f}|_C = 4g+12-4f, hence deg W_4 = 20 and deg W_5 = 16 at g=6; this line, the Serre-duality step H^1(C,W|_C(-Gamma)) = H^0(C, omega_C (x) W|_C^vee(Gamma))^vee, the threshold 4f+n-2g-14, and the normalization O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C = omega_C (x) gamma^*omega_{P^1}^vee were re-verified live against the ar5iv rendering of arXiv:2208.02357v2 Section 10 and agree with the packet's verbatim locator excerpt. (1) Since 20 > 2g-2 = 10 and 16 > 10, h^1(W_4) = h^1(W_5) = 0 on every geometric fibre, so h^0(W) = 15+11 = 26 is constant, pi_*W is locally free of rank 26 and commutes with base change, and pi_*(W|_Gamma) is locally free of rank 2*6 = 12; thus phi (x) k(b) is the fibre evaluation map for every b. (2) f=4 component: deg(omega_C (x) W_4^vee(Gamma)) = 10-20+6 = -4 < 0, so coker(phi_4) = 0 (independently reproving FND-0062); equivalently H^1(W_4(-Gamma)) = 0 since deg W_4(-Gamma) = 14 > 10. (3) f=5 component: N := omega_C (x) W_5^vee(Gamma) has degree 10-16+6 = 0, exactly the borderline recorded by FND-0074 (n-6 at g=6, f=5), so h^0(N) in {0,1} with h^0(N) = 1 iff N = O_C iff O_C(Gamma) = L := W_5 (x) omega_C^{-1} (FND-0063). Because h^1(W_5) = 0, coker(phi_5) = H^1(W_5(-Gamma)) = H^0(N)^vee, of dimension h^0(N) <= 1; hence rank(phi_5) = 6 - h^0(N) in {5,6}. (4) The snake lemma applied to the filtration, using R^1 pi_* W_4 = 0 and coker(phi_4) = 0 (the two degree vanishings that FND-0099 demands be cited), gives coker(phi) = coker(phi_5), so rank(phi) = 12 - h^0(N) in {11,12}. The finding's stated reason -- the cokernel is Serre-dual to H^0 of a degree-zero line bundle -- is exactly correct and is the load-bearing step. (5) Ideal-theoretic conclusion, verified against primary reference rather than asserted: with target locally free of rank 12, I_{12-k}(phi) = Fit_k(coker phi) (Stacks Project Section 15.8, tag 07Z6, Lemma 15.8.2 defining Fit_k by (n-k)x(n-k) minors of a presentation); formation commutes with arbitrary base change (Lemma 15.8.4(3), tag 07ZA); and Lemma 15.8.7 (tag 07ZC) states Fit_k(M) not contained in p iff dim_{kappa(p)} M (x) kappa(p) <= k. Since dim coker(phi) (x) kappa(b) = h^0(N_b) <= 1 at every point b of B, Fit_1(coker phi) = I_11(phi) is contained in no prime, i.e. I_11(phi) = O_B; identically I_5(phi_5) = Fit_1(coker phi_5) = O_B. All three assertions of FND-0122 are therefore correct. SCOPE SHARPENINGS (none of which weakens the finding). (a) 'Locally Noetherian' is unnecessary: tag 07ZC is a prime-by-prime statement over an arbitrary ring and minors commute with arbitrary base change, so the conclusion holds over any base, including non-reduced ones -- and non-reducedness is precisely harmless here because the criterion is applied at residue fields, not at reduced points. (b) 'Six pairwise-disjoint sections' is stronger than used: only flatness and relative degree 6 of Gamma enter, so the statement holds for any relative effective Cartier divisor of degree 6; disjointness is load-bearing for the S_6-torsor of FND-0064/FND-0075, not for the rank bounds. (c) Two hypotheses are implicit and must be carried: all geometric fibres smooth of genus 6, and fibrewise balancedness of F -- both are needed for deg W_4 = 20 > 2g-2 and deg W_5 = 16 > 10; on an unbalanced fibre (f_1 <= 3) deg W_4 >= 24 still exceeds 10 but the labels and the degree-zero coincidence for W_5 fail, so the finding must not be quoted outside the balanced locus. (d) phi must be the curve-level evaluation pi_*(W|_C) -> pi_*(W|_Gamma) of FND-0097/FND-0099. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 states its evaluation map on the ambient P(E^vee), factored as H^0(P(E^vee),W) -> H^0(C,W|_C) -> H^0(Gamma,W|_Gamma); the rank bounds proved here concern only the second arrow, and transporting them to the ambient composite additionally requires H^1(P(E^vee), W (x) I_C) = 0, which this audit does not verify. (e) The value set {11,12} is sharp and both values occur: the rank-11 locus is exactly V(Fit_0) = V(I_12(phi)), the Abel-Jacobi incidence locus which FND-0096 identifies universally with I_e and which FND-0005 shows is nonempty (subject to FND-0083's caveat that fibrewise nonemptiness of the reduced-support/ordered model is a separate question). WHAT THE FINDING DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It collapses the C66-COMP-RANK deliverable 'compute determinantal rank-drop ideals' to a single nontrivial Fitting ideal Fit_0 = I_12(phi) = I_6(phi_5): the rank stratification has exactly two strata, there is no deeper degeneracy stratum, and no component of Z can be supported on a rank <= 10 locus. It is a genuine exception to the FND-0046 caution that fibrewise equivalences give equality only on geometric points -- the unit-ideal conclusion is the one case where fibrewise rank data does pin the ideal sheaf globally, because V(I) = empty forces I = O_B -- and it must not be over-read as licensing any scheme-theoretic identification of Z: Fit_0 remains the substantive object and FND-0046/FND-0047/FND-0107 continue to apply there. Cross-check with FND-0068: the generic determinantal expectation for a one-step rank drop of a 26x12 map is (26-11)(12-11) = 15, whereas the actual locus has codimension 6 in the Pic^0 direction (FND-0096); FND-0122 is consistent with FND-0068 and strengthens the picture by showing the deeper expected loci are empty rather than merely of excess dimension. DISTINCTNESS / NO MERGE. Distinct from FND-0062 (f=4 obstruction vanishes), FND-0063 (f=5 degree-zero Abel-Jacobi criterion), FND-0074 (borderline n=6 and non-transport), FND-0096 (Fit_0 = I_e universally), and FND-0097/FND-0099 (filtered reduction and Fit_0(coker phi) = Fit_0(coker phi_5)): each of those concerns the single Fitting ideal Fit_0 or its inputs, while FND-0122 is the only record asserting triviality of the deeper minor ideals and the two-stratum rank stratification.
